message.reasoning:
The user wants a complete single-file HTML tic-tac-toe game with an unbeatable minimax AI. I want this to feel crafted, not templated: a distinctive design. Tic-tac-toe — what's characteristic? The grid, the chalk/pencil marks, X and O strokes, the game-tree of minimax. I could open with a game-tree visualization or a big interactive board as the hero rather than a generic banner.

Let me design something bold: an arcade/parlor feel with a paper-and-ink drafting aesthetic. I want a distinctive display face paired with a readable body face. Display face: something with character. Options: "Bricolage Grotesque", "Fraunces", "Instrument Serif", "Space Grotesk", "Archivo Black", "Chivo Mono", "Syne", "Bricolage". Let's pick something with personality: "Bricolage Grotesque" for display and "Newsreader" or "Spline Sans" for body. Or a technical/blueprint vibe: "Space Mono" + "Sora".

Idea: A "minimax laboratory" — the board is the hero, huge, off-center, with a live game-tree explorer panel showing the minimax search evaluating positions. That's characteristic of tic-tac-toe AND of minimax. Ambient background: subtle grid paper with faint animated scanlines / drifting node-link diagram.

Layout: asymmetric two-column. Left: giant board with hand-drawn-ish strokes (SVG X and O with stroke-dashoffset draw animation). Right: a stack of living elements:
- Score tally (You / AI / Draws) with animated counters
- Minimax search readout: live list of candidate moves with scores, depth, and a bar showing eval — updates as AI searches (simulate with small delay stepping through nodes)
- Game tree mini-visualization (SVG) that lights up as nodes are explored
- Difficulty selector (since AI is unbeatable, offer "Novice / Tactician / Flawless" where Flawless = full minimax — but the request says unbeatable AI, so default Flawless; difficulty is a bonus, keep it)
- Move log / status ticker

Top: a slim masthead with the title in a bold display face, and a "who's turn" indicator.

Also: a "first move" choice, side choice (X/O), win-line drawing animation, confetti-ish? Maybe a subtle stroke flourish.

Interactions:
- Hover on cells: ghost mark preview with low opacity
- Click: place mark with draw animation
- AI thinking: brief delay with "searching" progress and node counter ticking
- Win: winning line drawn across board, cells pulse, banner
- Keyboard support: 1-9 keys, arrow keys + enter
- Sound: tiny WebAudio blips (optional, toggleable) — adds "alive" feel. Keep it subtle and default on? Better default off? I'll include a sound toggle default on but very quiet... Actually autoplay policies require user gesture; fine since sounds only trigger on interaction.

- Scroll reveal: a section below explaining minimax with an animated pseudocode block and a small tree diagram. Keep it tasteful — a "How the machine thinks" section with the actual minimax code and an interactive depth demo. That adds richness.

Palette: I want something with character that isn't just a flat light surface with one bright accent, and not the usual indigo/violet gradients. Let's do a deep teal-ink base with warm paper board and coral/amber marks. I'll use a multi-hue palette: ink navy #0d1b2a-ish, teal, warm cream board, X in coral-red #ff5a5f, O in amber/gold #ffb703, plus a mint accent. Several hues keeps it lively.

Actually let's do: background = deep slate-teal (#0b1f24 → #103038 gradient with grain + faint grid), board = warm off-white paper panel (#f4efe6) with soft shadow, X = vermillion (#e04a3f), O = deep teal ink (#0f4c5c) or amber. Text on dark = #e8f1ef. Accent = chartreuse? Let's use amber #f2b134 for highlights and mint #6fd3c7.

Type: Display = "Bricolage Grotesque" (variable, quirky) — good. Body = "Spline Sans" or "IBM Plex Sans"? Let's use "Spline Sans" for body and "Spline Sans Mono" for data readouts. Three families from Google Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque (display), Spline Sans (body), Spline Sans Mono (mono). That's a nice pairing.

Hmm, keep font loading
